papers.title: Observation of Polarization Topology in Magneto-Optical BICs
papers.abstract: Polarization topology in momentum space is a fundamental characteristic of photonic bound states in the continuum (BICs), where the winding of far-field polarization defines a quantized topological charge. Although magneto-optical (MO) BICs combine polarization topology with magnetically tunable chirality, experimental characterization remains challenging because time-reversal symmetry (TRS) breaking complicates eigenpolarization extraction. Here, we experimentally resolve the momentum-space polarization topology of an MO BIC by reconstructing its two-dimensional far-field eigenpolarization texture. We extract the resonant output polarization using singular value decomposition of the polarization-resolved angle-resolved reflection matrix without invoking reciprocity. The reconstructed polarization azimuth winds counterclockwise by 2 $π$ around the $Γ$-point singularity, yielding a topological charge of q = +1. Moreover, the polarization handedness can be reversed solely by varying the magnetic-bias strength, while the field direction and the measured topological charge remain unchanged. A non-Hermitian coupled-mode model traces this reversal to hybridization between the BIC mode and a leaky mode. This work establishes experimental access to momentum-space polarization topology in nonreciprocal photonics, opening a route to explore topological singularities and their evolution under active TRS breaking.

papers.title: The Impact of Markovian Errors on Random Circuits
papers.abstract: Randomized benchmarking (RB) returns a single decay parameter or gate error rate, but when the noise is gate-dependent that parameter is notoriously difficult to interpret. We study RB and related random-circuit benchmarks under small gate-local Markovian noise by factorizing each noisy gate into its ideal action followed by the exponential of a small error generator and then perturbing the RB $\mathscr{L}$ matrix, which models the RB decay. For any low-error gate set that satisfies the requirements of RB (it is a sequence-asymptotic unitary 2-design), we show that Pauli-stochastic error rates contribute linearly to the RB decay parameter, while Hamiltonian error rates contribute through a gauge-invariant quadratic form. Pauli-correlation and active generators are absent from the linear term and enter only at higher order. For the single-qubit native gate set $\{X_{π/2},Y_{π/2}\}$ we derive this quadratic form explicitly in terms of three first-order gauge-invariant (FOGI) coordinates: the two intrinsic over-rotations and one relational axis-tilt error. The resulting formula explains the dependence of DRB on the sampling distribution and the compilation dependence of CRB. These results turn RB decay rates into interpretable functions of experimentally meaningful elementary error rates.

papers.title: DuoCook: An Overcooked-Inspired Benchmark for Visual Planning and Coordination
papers.abstract: Coordinating two players in a cooking task requires a vision-language agent to track changing scene states, sequence recipe steps, and allocate shared resources under a time budget. We introduce an Overcooked-inspired benchmark for evaluating these capabilities in Unreal Engine environments constructed using coding agents. A single vision-language model controls both players from top-down visual observations, selecting high-level actions while the engine executes navigation. The benchmark contains 20 maps in five categories. These categories support evaluation of centralized coordination under equipment contention, changing terrain, and handoff dependencies. A prop legend and pot ingredient-count indicators provide explicit visual cues, while grid-based destinations support spatial grounding. The evaluation compares four VLMs on all 20 maps, measuring task score, order completion, delivery precision, action acceptance rate, and model API expenditure. A memory ablation on the same 20 maps examines the effect of a shared, self-authored notebook while retaining six-response action history in both conditions. The strongest evaluated model, \texttt{gpt-6-astra}, achieves 26.2\% mean order completion. Notebook memory has mixed score effects across models, with positive mean differences for Claude and Qwen and negative differences for GPT and Gemini.

papers.title: SCOPE: Scene-graph Construction Optimized by Plan Error-correction for Robot Long-term Planning Datasets
papers.abstract: Task and Motion Planning (TAMP) stands as a fundamental challenge in robotics, essential for enabling autonomous agents to execute complex, long-horizon tasks in diverse environments. While Large Language Models (LLMs) introduce a new paradigm for TAMP by leveraging extensive common sense, their inherent reasoning limitations hinder direct application, and fine-tuning strategies to enhance these capabilities are currently bottlenecked by the scarcity of high-quality datasets. Existing automated generation methods often suffer from homogeneity, limiting model generalization, and unsolvability, where hallucinated scene graphs create physical mismatches with task goals. To address these issues, we propose Scene-graph Construction Optimized by Plan Error-correction (SCOPE), an automated framework designed to generate diverse and executable TAMP datasets. SCOPE incorporates multi-level diversity metrics to maximize the information entropy of scenarios. Crucially, it introduces a Plan Feedback Error-correction pipeline that utilizes planner execution failures as feedback signals to retroactively rectify logical inconsistencies in scene graphs, ensuring physical feasibility. Experimental results demonstrate that SCOPE exhibits greater robustness to erroneous scene graphs and generates higher-quality data. When utilized for LLM fine-tuning, SCOPE-generated data yield a downstream TAMP model that achieves an absolute 12.33% gain in success rate over its counterpart fine-tuned with data generated by DELTA, a state-of-the-art PDDL-based planner.

papers.title: Short curves in homogeneous spaces of the unitary group for unitarily invariant norms
papers.abstract: Let A be a unital *-subalgebra of $M_n(C)$ and let $M = U(n)/U(A)$, with the quotient Finsler metric induced by a unitarily invariant norm on $u(n)$, normalized so that $||iP|| = 1$ for rank-one projections $P$. This family contains the unitary orbits of Hermitian matrices, in particular flag manifolds and Grassmann manifolds. We prove that if $z_0$ is a minimal lifting of a tangent vector $X$ with $||X||_{\infty} < π/2$ , then the one-parameter group $t \mapsto e^{t z_0}\cdot o$ has minimal length among all piecewise smooth curves in $M$ joining its endpoints. The same holds in manifolds $N=SU(n)/(SU(n) \cap A)$ for every Ad-invariant Finsler norm on $su(n)$, not necessarily symmetric (i.e. the unit sphere does not need to be balanced). The proof relies on the convexity of the distance from the identity along geodesic segments, valid for all these norms. We also prove that the ball of radius $π/2$ around the identity, for the spectral norm, is convex along one-parameter segments. This extends known results for the p-Schatten norms with p even, and gives a new proof for the operator norm, where the result is due to Duran, Mata-Lorenzo and Recht.

papers.title: Dispersive Tree Agreements for Multi-Robot Coordination
papers.abstract: Multi-robot coordination of nonlinear systems is naturally formulated as joint-space optimal control subject to constraints over groups of robots. Existing methods that approach joint optimality remain largely centralized, offline, and confined to collision-free motion planning, while decentralized, real-time counterparts target safe navigation without pursuing the joint optimum. This paper develops a decentralized, real-time planner that approaches the joint optimum as an anytime process. We extend a recent single-robot framework that searches dispersive trees of forward-propagated commands for differentially flat systems to coordinate a multi-robot team near-optimally. We first show that the inter-robot coupling can be effectively replaced by some local constraints, under which locally grown dispersive trees contain a near-optimal agreement. It is this structure that the robots pursue by decentralized column generation, negotiating rents on the shared space that guide the search of each robot's tree. The negotiation settles on an agreement whose near-optimality is certified at quiescence. Our protocol, WarpWeaver, implements this negotiation as an asynchronous real-time loop over a receding horizon, and demonstrates effective closure to quiesced agreements even when real-time deadlines cut the negotiation short. In simulation, WarpWeaver reduces total travel time by up to 22% against centralized offline planners on the Dynobench suite and by up to 37% against a decentralized real-time baseline, and nearly doubles the success rate of a task-specific planner on graph connectivity. Hardware experiments on six robots planning onboard demonstrate real-world implementability.

papers.title: Squaring-the-Sphere: Distortion-Free and Seamless Panorama Generation via CubeAtlas
papers.abstract: Generating 360-degree panoramas requires both local perspective fidelity and global spherical continuity. Existing representations face a trade-off: equirectangular projection (ERP) enables seamless panorama modeling but suffers from severe distortion and a domain gap to pre-trained image generators, whereas cubemaps preserve perspective geometry but often produce inconsistent faces and visible seams. We present Squaring-the-Sphere, a panoramic image generation framework built on a novel representation CubeAtlas, which unfolds all cubemap faces into a single compact canvas. By arranging orientation-aligned, rotated polar regions alongside the equatorial faces, this representation preserves the perspective geometry of cubemaps while organizing the cross-face relationships required for seamless panorama assembly. It further enables a pretrained diffusion transformer to model the complete panorama jointly in a single pass, without altering the backbone architecture or positional encoding. While CubeAtlas has a token count comparable to ERP, its structured layout makes many dense attention interactions unnecessary. We therefore introduce a layout-aware sparse attention mask that preserves the interactions required for panorama continuity while removing geometrically irrelevant token pairs. As a result, CubeAtlas achieves better quality than ERP modeling with lower attention computation. Furthermore, we introduce a training-free super-resolution technique and a fusion scheme that enhance fine details in distortion-free perspective space before achieving the final ERP panorama. Experiments on various benchmarks demonstrate that our method improves geometric fidelity, cross-view consistency, and high-resolution visual quality over previous methods.

papers.title: Geometry-Dependent Properties of Physically Crosslinked PPy-PVA Hydrogels Enable Tunable Iontophoretic Drug Delivery
papers.abstract: Objective: Iontophoretic drug delivery has primarily relied on current modulation to regulate drug transport. Here, we investigate hydrogel geometry, microstructure, and local electric fields as alternative mechanisms for controlling transdermal delivery. Methods: Bovine serum albumin (BSA) was encapsulated in polypyrrole-polyvinyl alcohol (PPy-PVA) hydrogels. Five geometries, including Hilbert curve-based designs, were fabricated to vary pore architecture and local electric field distributions. We optimized PPy content, drug loading, and current density. Electric fields were evaluated using finite element analysis, and microstructures were characterized by scanning electron microscopy. Drug transport was assessed using Franz diffusion cells with artificial membranes. Results: Hydrogel geometries exhibited distinct microstructures and electric field distributions. Iontophoresis substantially enhanced permeability compared with passive diffusion, while individual geometries produced different cumulative release, flux, and permeability profiles. The average iontophoretic permeability was (3.80 +/- 1.93) x 10^-5, exceeding previously reported values using artificial membranes. Conclusion: Geometry-driven fabrication of drug-loaded hydrogels enables tunable transport characteristics under both iontophoretic and passive conditions. Significance: Geometry-mediated control offers an alternative approach to regulating iontophoretic drug delivery without requiring individual current-density modulation.

papers.title: Mixed State Deep Thermalization under Generic Quantum Errors
papers.abstract: Pure-state deep thermalization predicts that, after sufficient scrambling, projected ensembles approach universal distributions that contain information beyond the reduced density matrix. In realistic quantum systems, however, noise is unavoidable and the projected states are generally mixed. Whether mixed-state deep thermalization admits an analogous universal limiting distribution has remained unclear. Here we answer this question for quantum dynamics containing local quantum channels, i.e., errors. We show that the late-time mixed-state projected ensemble is completely determined by the normalized Choi state of the error channel and is universal, independent of the microscopic details of the underlying unitary dynamics. We establish this result analytically for dual-unitary circuits, global Haar-random dynamics, and local Haar-random circuits at large local dimension, and verify it numerically in qubit circuits and kicked Ising dynamics. In a solvable setting, we further find exponentially fast convergence to the limiting ensemble. Our results extend deep thermalization to noisy quantum dynamics and establish a direct correspondence between quantum errors and universal random mixed-state ensembles.

papers.title: A Subjective Bayesian Approach to Address Unchecked Assumptions in a Causal Analysis
papers.abstract: Causal analyses using observational data rely on identifying assumptions that cannot be verified from the observed data alone. When such unchecked assumptions fail, effect estimates may be biased and uncertainty may be understated. We propose the Adjusted Model for Unchecked Assumptions (AMUA), a subjective Bayesian framework that propagates uncertainty about the joint validity of key causal assumptions through a two-component posterior mixture. One component corresponds to the standard observational causal model in which the assumptions hold (referred to as the "assumption-hold component"); the other represents a flexibly defined model that allows the causal assumptions to fail (referred to as the "assumption-fail component"). The mixture weight $π$ is specified by the analyst as the prior probability assigned to the assumption-hold component. This formulation leads to a new diagnostic, $π_{\min}$: the smallest value of $π$ for which the 95\% HPD set for the average treatment effect (ATE) excludes zero. In simulations with a spatially structured unmeasured confounder, we evaluate bias, interval length, and coverage as $π$ varies. The results show that acknowledging assumption uncertainty can widen intervals, and improve coverage relative to analyses that treat the assumptions as certain. In a county-level application relating long-term PM$_{2.5}$ exposure to COVID-19 mortality, AMUA shows how posterior conclusions depend on prior confidence in the identifying assumptions.

papers.title: DiffDreamer: Coupling World Models with Differentiable Simulation for Agile Quadrotor Control
papers.abstract: Tasks such as quadrotor dynamic-gate racing require agents to anticipate external motion while maintaining precise high-frequency control. World-model-based reinforcement learning provides a natural solution by learning latent dynamics for future imagination, yet it often entangles environmental evolution and the robot's own dynamics in a single learned rollout, where model bias can affect policy optimization efficiency. We propose DiffDreamer, a differentiable reinforcement learning framework that tightly couples a learned world model with differentiable simulation for actor optimization. In one optimization step, the learned world model propagates latent states that capture external dynamics and history-dependent features, while the differentiable simulator propagates the robot's explicit physical state. We further decompose the actor objective into a critic-driven pathway for non-differentiable task rewards and a simulator-driven pathway for differentiable motion rewards. Experiments on aggressive tracking and dynamic-gate racing show that DiffDreamer improves training convergence over the model-free, model-based, and differentiable-RL baselines, and final performance over these baselines and classical planning and control methods. Additional experiments assess reward decomposition and the odometry-conditioned relative-state representation through ablations. We also provide proof-of-concept real-world flight experiments for validation.

papers.title: F2G-Pose: Geometry-Aware Foundation Feature Lifting for Direct RGB-D Category-Level Object Pose Estimation
papers.abstract: This paper studies category-level RGB-D object pose estimation, which recovers an object's 3D rotation and translation without instance-specific CAD models or reference views. This task is highly ambiguous due to intra-class variations, symmetries, and partial observations. Current solutions struggle to balance reliability and efficiency: methods based on intermediate structures are prone to error propagation, while diffusion models suffer from high inference latency and complex post-hoc candidate extraction. To address this, we present F2G-Pose, a real-time direct, single-pass framework that predicts category-level pose, metric size, and camera-frame completed shape from a single RGB-D observation in one feed-forward pass. F2G-Pose lifts dense visual foundation features to partial point clouds, encodes local geometry with DGCNN tokenization, and integrates object-level structure with a Mixture-of-Experts Transformer. Joint size prediction and camera-frame shape completion encourage metric consistency through dense geometric supervision. With its task-specific network trained only on pose-annotated synthetic SOPE data and its frozen RADIO backbone externally pretrained, F2G-Pose achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on SOPE and ROPE while running at 28 FPS for pose-only inference, and further demonstrates strong camera-frame geometry on HouseCat6D and real-object transfer on HANDAL. Analyses of latency, robustness, shape completion, and GenPose++ candidate behavior further demonstrate the efficiency and reliability of F2G-Pose, with real-world manipulation experiments demonstrating deployment potential under segmented RGB-D inputs. The project page, code, and pretrained models are made available at this https URL .

papers.title: HiP3R: Hierarchical Pose Graphs for Long-Horizon 3D Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Feed-forward models accurately estimate camera motion and 3D geometry from short video windows. However, computational and memory costs prevent direct inference on sequences containing thousands of frames. Long videos must therefore be processed as overlapping chunks. This division produces independent local reconstructions with inconsistent coordinate frames and duplicate estimates of shared cameras. Achieving global consistency requires propagating constraints from adjacent overlaps and distant revisits across the sequence. This requirement naturally motivates pose graph optimization. However, the choice of graph level creates a trade-off. Chunk-level graphs efficiently resolve scale drift and close large loops. Yet, their rigid transformations cannot correct internal errors or conflicting frame predictions. Conversely, frame-level optimization offers local flexibility, but scaling it globally is computationally expensive and can break metric scale. HiP3R resolves this trade-off using a hierarchical pose graph. HiP3R first optimizes a robust chunk-level $\mathrm{Sim}(3)$ graph to establish the global layout and scale. It then holds this layout fixed and estimates one shared $\mathrm{SE}(3)$ camera per frame, turning overlapping window predictions into a single trajectory. Experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of HiP3R in improving camera trajectories and 3D reconstruction. Our method applies to both chunk-based and streaming backends without additional training or fine-tuning. The codes are available at this https URL .

papers.title: OmniRay: Camera-Agnostic Monocular 3D Reconstruction with Composite Ray Fields
papers.abstract: Monocular models recover 3D geometry from a single image in one pass, but most assume a pinhole camera and produce distorted geometry on the wide-angle imagery produced by fisheye and panoramic lenses. Camera-aware models remove this assumption by predicting a per-pixel ray field. However, they represent different camera geometries using a single fixed basis to capture both the overall camera projection and its finer variations. We argue that camera geometry can be viewed as having a hierarchy of complexity for representing rays. We present OmniRay, a feed-forward model whose Ray Module is composed of three components: a monotone radial base that captures radially symmetric structure, a spherical-harmonic residual for smooth deviations from it, and a free-form residual for remaining local variation. These components are composed as successive rotations on the sphere, allowing the representation to accommodate diverse camera geometries. Given a single image, OmniRay predicts a ray direction and an up-to-scale radial distance for every pixel, from which a 3D point cloud is recovered without needing camera information at inference time. Extensive experiments across different camera configurations demonstrate that OmniRay establishes a new state-of-the-art in camera-agnostic monocular 3D reconstruction.

papers.title: Odd radio circle J1555+2726: Observational evidence for shock re-acceleration of fossil plasma
papers.abstract: Context. Odd radio circles (ORCs) are peculiar extragalactic sources recently discovered. They are characterised by one or more bright rings extending on scales of hundreds of kiloparsecs, and are filled with fainter emission. A massive elliptical galaxy lies at the centre of ORCs. While their formation mechanism is debated, a shock is plausibly involved. Aims. We aim to constrain the nature of ORC J1555+2726 (ORC4) through the analysis of its morphological and spectral properties. Methods. We utilised Low Frequency ARray (LOFAR), upgraded Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (uGMRT), and MeerKAT radio data at 50-1284 MHz to obtain images and spectral index maps at high resolution and sensitivity. Results. Both the resolution and observing frequency affect the observed morphology. In particular, the brightness contrast between the ring and the filling emission becomes progressively smoother from higher to lower frequencies. We measured an integrated spectrum of slope $\alpha=1.06\pm 0.03$, a radio power of $P_{\rm 150}= (5.4\pm 0.5)\times 10^{25} \; {\rm W \; Hz^{-1}}$ at 150 MHz, and a radial spectral flattening down to $\alpha\sim0.5$ at the ring location. However, we inferred a negative (convex) spectral curvature and a peculiar spectral shape in radio colour-colour diagrams, which imply spectral flattening towards high frequencies. These properties cannot be explained by shock acceleration of thermal particles and standard ageing. Conclusions. The observed features suggest that a mixture of electrons with different spectra coexist within ORC4 volume, likely associated with shock re-acceleration of a fossil relativistic reservoir. The ring emission is plausibly dominated by higher-energy electrons re-accelerated at the shock front, while lower-energy re-accelerated electrons are more uniformly distributed across the whole source (possibly ellipsoidal) volume.

papers.title: Reading, Writing, Sharing, and Interacting with the World through Video
papers.abstract: Video foundation models have advanced rapidly in understanding and generating visual sequences, while video world models seek to capture the underlying dynamics of the world they depict. Despite their different objectives, both concern the relationship between video observations and an evolving world. This survey adopts world modeling as a unifying lens for examining these developments. Viewing an observed video as a partial, lossy, and temporally ordered projection of a latent temporal world, we organize the literature around four complementary operations: reading infers world properties from observed video; writing synthesizes video from specified or learned world conditions; sharing integrates understanding and generation through common modeling mechanisms; and interacting predicts and updates world states under actions and evolving observations. This perspective distinguishes temporal coherence in observed or generated sequences from consistency in the underlying world state. Across tasks, representations, models, datasets, and benchmarks, we trace a shift in emphasis from clip-level recognition and perceptual fidelity toward persistent state, controllable evolution, physical and causal validity, and evaluation grounded in interaction and downstream decisions, and we distill the open challenges that follow.

papers.title: Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success
papers.abstract: Robotic foundation models are typically evaluated through costly closed-loop rollouts, which motivates cheap offline proxies for model capability. The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) suggests that as representations improve, different modalities such as vision and language converge toward a shared statistical model of reality. We ask whether motion trajectories form another such modality: as embodied models become more capable, should their sensory representations converge toward the structure of physical motion? To examine this, we propose Sensorimotor Alignment ($S^2$), a training-free offline metric that measures how well a model's sensory representation aligns with the geometry of physical motion. We find that $S^2$ correlates positively with downstream robot task success across embodied model families, making it a low-cost offline proxy for prioritizing models before closed-loop evaluation. $S^2$ can also identify promising vision-language model (VLM) backbones even before costly fine-tuning into vision-language-action models (VLAs). Beyond this correlation, $S^2$ offers representation-level explanations for phenomena observed in VLAs and world action models (WAMs). With $S^2$, we extend PRH to embodied models and make sensorimotor alignment empirically measurable, offering insight into why an embodied model succeeds beyond its closed-loop success rate.
